name: agent-review-11-a-step-that-fails
goal: A confirmed step the route refuses, so the failed-step path is exercised rather than described.
brief: You want a link that has already stopped working, because you are testing what the clinic sees when a link expires.

messages.text: Give me a link to the Larkmead new patient sign-up that stopped working yesterday.

seed.requires: The form released to test with one link on it, and the signed-in person holding Publish forms for test.

assistantMust: say plainly that the step did not run and that the reason is on the card beside it
not invent a cause and not guess at one
read its own earlier words back when asked why it stopped, rather than composing a new reason
offer the next move, which is a link with an expiry that has not passed

notes: Scenario 3 is the same question over a step that never ran. This one is the other half: the route refuses an expiry in the past at Confirm, so a step genuinely fails and the card carries the reason. Turn 1 states no card count because both endings pass: a card whose step then fails, or a decline up front with the reason. Turn 2 states none at all, because a question about what already happened is answered from the conversation. What fails is a confirmed failure the reply does not own, a reason invented rather than read back, or a second link minted to paper over it.
